Q180.L1t: Photographs offered at trial are a form of demonstrative or real evidence that must be authenticated before a court admits them.
Q180.L2t: Authentication of a photograph does not require that the person who took it testify, because any witness with knowledge of the scene may authenticate it.
Q180.L3t: A photograph is authenticated by testimony from a witness with knowledge that it is a fair and accurate representation of the subject it depicts, and the photographer here only identified the prints as the ones she took and gave to the owner.
Q180.L4t: The photographs should be excluded because no witness testified that they fairly and accurately show the ruptured tank.
Q180.L2f: Photographs can be authenticated only by the person who operated the camera, and no other witness with knowledge of the scene may do so.
Q180.L3f: Photographs are admissible only if the proponent shows an unbroken chain of custody for the film from the moment it was shot until it was developed, much as with physical evidence like drugs.
Q180.L4f: The photographs should be excluded because there was an unaccountable gap in the chain of custody between the taking of the photographs and the processing of the negatives.

Q181.L1t: Employment contracts are governed by general contract law, and courts review their terms individually for enforceability.
Q181.L2t: An at-will employment arrangement can be replaced by a written agreement that sets new terms, including a notice period for termination.
Q181.L3t: A clause that restricts competition after employment ends is enforceable only if it is reasonable in duration and geographic scope, and a bar on any aspect of the hardware business for two years across a 50-mile radius reaches further than the employer's legitimate interest in protecting its business.
Q181.L4t: The salary and the 60-day termination provisions would be enforced, but the covenant not to compete would not be enforced as written.
Q181.L2f: A written employment agreement signed after the employee has already worked for the employer is void for lack of any new consideration.
Q181.L3f: A court will enforce a non-compete covenant of any length and geographic reach so long as the employee signed it, and the only term likely to be struck down is the fixed $1,500 sum payable on breach.
Q181.L4f: The agreement would be enforced in full except for the $1,500 payment clause, which would be struck as an unenforceable penalty.

Q182.L1t: Future interests in land, such as remainders and reversions, are governed by common law rules on their creation, classification and transfer.
Q182.L2t: At common law the Rule Against Perpetuities voids a contingent interest that might vest more than twenty-one years after the lives in being at its creation.
Q182.L3t: The remainder to the neighbor and her heirs was given to an ascertained, living person with no condition precedent, so it was vested at creation, and a vested remainder is not subject to the Rule and passes by will when its holder dies.
Q182.L4t: The friend holds only a life estate, and the remainder passed under the neighbor's will to the charity as a vested remainder.
Q182.L2f: The woman's conveyance to the friend for life created a life estate that could be transferred to others only with the consent of the remainderman.
Q182.L3f: The remainder to the neighbor and her heirs was contingent because the heirs could not be known until her death, so it could vest too remotely and was therefore invalid under the Rule Against Perpetuities.
Q182.L4f: The friend holds a life estate and the woman keeps a reversion, because the neighbor's remainder is void under the Rule Against Perpetuities.
